gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Thinkware's multiplexer records every add-on camera (both exterior side cameras and the rear camera) into one shared 1920 × 1080, 30 fps file that cannot be saved separately. So the 'ARC800 + exterior side cameras' setup ChatGPT called premium gives each side view only part of a single 1080p frame, not its own 1080p recording.
standout_why: I compared against the page ChatGPT cited, the Thinkware Help Center article 'How to Install the Multiplexer box'. It lists compatible models (ARC 800 included), says 3-, 4- or 5-channel setups are possible, and says to cut the white wire to make a side camera record the right side. It says nothing about the add-on views sharing one file or one 1080p/30 fps frame. ChatGPT's answer describes the ARC800 setup only as 'dedicated exterior left/right cameras' with 'better physical positioning' and never mentions the shared frame. I could not open Car and Driver (the fetch was blocked) or DashCamTalk within the call budget, so I can't rule out that they mention it. Thinkware's own multiplexer product page gives only 'Composite Video: Full HD (1920 x 1080) @ 30fps'. The 'merged together and saved into one video file' wording is on Thinkware's multi-channel category page, which no result ChatGPT got points to.
decides: It weakens ChatGPT's 'best premium' Thinkware pick for sideswipe evidence. That route costs ARC 800 $279.99 + Multiplexer Box $99.99 + Exterior Side View Cameras (pack of 2) $159.98 = $539.96 on thinkwarestore.com on 2026-11-21, before a hardwiring cable for parking mode. All of that buys side views that share one 1080p/30 fps composite with the rear camera. Thinkware's own side-camera pack page also leaves the ARC 800 off its compatibility list, while the multiplexer page includes it. All-in-one 4-channel cams record each side as its own channel instead: per our Dealectric record, the Botslab G980H records rear, left and right at 1080p each, at 25 fps, next to a 3K front. That supports Botslab as the pick for in-cabin side coverage at well under half the price. Thinkware still wins on one thing: its exterior, IP68-style side cameras sit outside the glass, so tint and window reflections don't apply. For a shopper who mainly wants door-ding evidence while parked, that is Thinkware's honest segment. Before using the Botslab per-channel claim I could not open botslab.com (HTTP 429 three times), so it needs a source read first.
